P1● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

Which of the following lists is an AP?

every difference must be the same (Topic 2). Why it applies: this is the AP test.

The differences −16-\dfrac{1}{6}−61​, −112-\dfrac{1}{12}−121​, … shrink; the denominators going up by 1 does not make the fractions an AP.
Constant difference 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​.
Each term doubles; the differences are 2, 4, 8.
The differences are 0, 1, 0.

Given: four lists. Asked: the one that is an AP.

Concept used: every difference must be the same (Topic 2). Why it applies: this is the AP test.

  1. 1

    Option (b) in quarters: 34,44,54,64\dfrac{3}{4}, \dfrac{4}{4}, \dfrac{5}{4}, \dfrac{6}{4}43​,44​,45​,46​ — each difference is 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​.

  2. 2

    Option (a): 13−12=−16\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{6}31​−21​=−61​ but 14−13=−112\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{3} = -\dfrac{1}{12}41​−31​=−121​ — not equal.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (b) ✔ Constant difference 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​.
    • (a) ✘ The differences −16-\dfrac{1}{6}−61​, −112-\dfrac{1}{12}−121​, … shrink; the denominators going up by 1 does not make the fractions an AP.
    • (c) ✘ Each term doubles; the differences are 2, 4, 8.
    • (d) ✘ The differences are 0, 1, 0.

  3. Check: 32=34+3×14\dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{3}{4} + 3 \times \dfrac{1}{4}23​=43​+3×41​ ✔.

  4. Answer (b)

    Common trap: Choosing (a) because "the bottom numbers go up by 1".
P2● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

The 15th term of the AP 6,10,14,…6, 10, 14, \ldots6,10,14,… is:

an=a+(n−1)da_n = a + (n - 1)dan​=a+(n−1)d (Topic 3). Why it applies: a, d and n are known.

a+nd=6+15×4a + nd = 6 + 15 \times 4a+nd=6+15×4: the 16th term.
n×d=15×4n \times d = 15 \times 4n×d=15×4; the first term is left out.
6+14×4=626 + 14 \times 4 = 626+14×4=62.
Uses d=6−10=−4d = 6 - 10 = -4d=6−10=−4: subtracted the wrong way round.

Given: a=6a = 6a=6, d=4d = 4d=4, n=15n = 15n=15. Asked: a15a_{15}a15​.

Concept used: an=a+(n−1)da_n = a + (n - 1)dan​=a+(n−1)d (Topic 3). Why it applies: a, d and n are known.

  1. 1

    a15=6+14×4=6+56=62a_{15} = 6 + 14 \times 4 = 6 + 56 = 62a15​=6+14×4=6+56=62.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (c) ✔ 6+14×4=626 + 14 \times 4 = 626+14×4=62.
    • (a) ✘ a+nd=6+15×4a + nd = 6 + 15 \times 4a+nd=6+15×4: the 16th term.
    • (b) ✘ n×d=15×4n \times d = 15 \times 4n×d=15×4; the first term is left out.
    • (d) ✘ Uses d=6−10=−4d = 6 - 10 = -4d=6−10=−4: subtracted the wrong way round.

  2. Check: 62−14×4=662 - 14 \times 4 = 662−14×4=6 ✔.

  3. Answer (c)

    Common trap: (a) — counting 15 steps from the first term instead of 14.
P3● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

Find the common difference and the next term of the AP 23,53,83,…2\sqrt{3}, 5\sqrt{3}, 8\sqrt{3}, \ldots23​,53​,83​,…

Full solution

Given: an AP of surds. Asked: d and the 4th term.

Concept used: d=a2−a1d = a_2 - a_1d=a2​−a1​; next term =a3+d= a_3 + d=a3​+d (Topic 2). Why it applies: the terms are multiples of 3\sqrt{3}3​.

  1. 1

    d=53−23=33d = 5\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}d=53​−23​=33​.

  2. 2

    Next term: 83+33=1138\sqrt{3} + 3\sqrt{3} = 11\sqrt{3}83​+33​=113​.

  3. Check: 83−53=338\sqrt{3} - 5\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}83​−53​=33​ as well ✔.

  4. Answer d=33d = 3\sqrt{3}d=33​; next term 11311\sqrt{3}113​

    Common trap: Writing d=3d = 3d=3 (forgetting the 3\sqrt{3}3​).

P4● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

For what value of x are x+3x + 3x+3, 2x+12x + 12x+1 and 4x−24x - 24x−2 three consecutive terms of an AP? Write the three terms.

Full solution

Given: three consecutive terms in x. Asked: x and the terms.

Concept used: 2b=a+c2b = a + c2b=a+c (Topic 2). Why it applies: the middle term is the average of its neighbours.

  1. 1

    Use 2b=a+c2b = a + c2b=a+c.

    2(2x+1)=(x+3)+(4x−2)2(2x + 1) = (x + 3) + (4x - 2)2(2x+1)=(x+3)+(4x−2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    Expand and collect.

    4x+2=5x+14x + 2 = 5x + 14x+2=5x+1Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Subtract 4x4x4x from both sides.

    2=x+12 = x + 12=x+1Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract 1 from both sides.

    x=1x = 1x=1Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    The terms: 1+3=41 + 3 = 41+3=4, 2+1=32 + 1 = 32+1=3, 4−2=24 - 2 = 24−2=2.

  6. Check: 4,3,24, 3, 24,3,2 — differences −1,−1-1, -1−1,−1 ✔.

  7. Answer x=1x = 1x=1; the terms are 4,3,24, 3, 24,3,2

    Common trap: Using 2a=b+c2a = b + c2a=b+c (the first term in the middle).

P6● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

A gardener plants 5 saplings on the first day, 8 on the second day, 11 on the third day, and so on. How many saplings does she plant on the 12th day?

one term = one day's planting; "on the 12th day" → a12a_{12}a12​ (Topic 5). Why it applies: the question is about a single day.

One term: a12=38a_{12} = 38a12​=38.
This is the total for the first 12 days, S12=6(10+33)=258S_{12} = 6(10 + 33) = 258S12​=6(10+33)=258.
a+nd=5+12×3a + nd = 5 + 12 \times 3a+nd=5+12×3: the 13th day.
n×d=12×3n \times d = 12 \times 3n×d=12×3; the 5 saplings of day 1 are missing.

Given: saplings per day 5,8,11,…5, 8, 11, \ldots5,8,11,…: a=5a = 5a=5, d=3d = 3d=3. Asked: the number on day 12 (one term).

Concept used: one term = one day's planting; "on the 12th day" → a12a_{12}a12​ (Topic 5). Why it applies: the question is about a single day.

  1. 1

    a12=5+11×3=38a_{12} = 5 + 11 \times 3 = 38a12​=5+11×3=38.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ One term: a12=38a_{12} = 38a12​=38.
    • (b) ✘ This is the total for the first 12 days, S12=6(10+33)=258S_{12} = 6(10 + 33) = 258S12​=6(10+33)=258.
    • (c) ✘ a+nd=5+12×3a + nd = 5 + 12 \times 3a+nd=5+12×3: the 13th day.
    • (d) ✘ n×d=12×3n \times d = 12 \times 3n×d=12×3; the 5 saplings of day 1 are missing.

  2. Check: day 12 is 11 steps of 3 after day 1: 5+33=385 + 33 = 385+33=38 ✔.

  3. Answer (a)

    Common trap: (b) — using SnS_nSn​ because the story is about many days. Read what is asked: on the 12th day.
P7● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

Find the sum of the first 15 odd natural numbers.

Full solution

Given: 1,3,5,…1, 3, 5, \ldots1,3,5,…; 15 terms. Asked: the sum.

Concept used: 1+3+⋯+(2n−1)=n21 + 3 + \cdots + (2n - 1) = n^21+3+⋯+(2n−1)=n2, or Sn=n2(a+l)S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l)Sn​=2n​(a+l) (Topic 4). Why it applies: the odd numbers form an AP with d=2d = 2d=2.

  1. 1

    The 15th odd number is 2×15−1=292 \times 15 - 1 = 292×15−1=29.

  2. 2

    S15=152(1+29)=15×15=225S_{15} = \dfrac{15}{2}(1 + 29) = 15 \times 15 = 225S15​=215​(1+29)=15×15=225.

  3. Check: 152=22515^2 = 225152=225 ✔.

  4. Answer 225225225

    Common trap: Taking the 15th odd number as 31 (2×15+12 \times 15 + 12×15+1), which gives 240.

P15●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

The sum of the first n terms of an AP is Sn=4n2−3nS_n = 4n^2 - 3nSn​=4n2−3n. Find its nth term, its common difference and its 20th term.

Full solution

Given: Sn=4n2−3nS_n = 4n^2 - 3nSn​=4n2−3n. Asked: ana_nan​, d, a20a_{20}a20​.

Concept used: an=Sn−Sn−1a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}an​=Sn​−Sn−1​, a1=S1a_1 = S_1a1​=S1​ (Topic 4). Why it applies: SnS_nSn​ is given as a formula.

  1. 1

    Replace n by n−1n - 1n−1 and expand.

    Sn−1=4(n−1)2−3(n−1)=4n2−11n+7S_{n-1} = 4(n - 1)^2 - 3(n - 1) = 4n^2 - 11n + 7Sn−1​=4(n−1)2−3(n−1)=4n2−11n+7Swipe to see the whole equation →

P30●●● AdvancedCase/source-based · 4 marksOriginal

Case: visitors to an exhibition

At a science exhibition, the total number of visitors in the first n days is 5n2+45n5n^2 + 45n5n2+45n.

(i) How many visitors came on the first day? (1)
(ii) Find the number of visitors on the nth day. (1)
(iii) (A) On which day did exactly 290 visitors come? (2)

OR
(iii) (B) How many visitors came in the first 10 days altogether, and how many on the 10th day? (2)

Full solution

Given: Sn=5n2+45nS_n = 5n^2 + 45nSn​=5n2+45n (a total). Asked: as above.

Concept used: a1=S1a_1 = S_1a1​=S1​, an=Sn−Sn−1a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}an​=Sn​−Sn−1​; term vs sum (Topics 4–5). Why it applies: the formula gives totals, but (i) and (iii)(A) ask about single days.

  1. 1

    (i) a1=S1=5+45=50a_1 = S_1 = 5 + 45 = 50a1​=S1​=5+45=50.

  2. 2

    (ii) an=[5n2+45n]−[5(n−1)2+45(n−1)]a_n = [5n^2 + 45n] - [5(n - 1)^2 + 45(n - 1)]an​=[5n2+45n]−[5(n−1)2+45(n−1)].

  3. 3

    Expand: 5(n−1)2+45(n−1)=5n2+35n−405(n - 1)^2 + 45(n - 1) = 5n^2 + 35n - 405(n−1)2+45(n−1)=5n2+35n−40; so an=10n+40a_n = 10n + 40an​=10n+40 (and a1=50a_1 = 50a1​=50 ✔).

  4. 4

    (iii)(A) 10n+40=29010n + 40 = 29010n+40=290, so 10n=25010n = 25010n=250 and n=25n = 25n=25.

  5. 5

    (iii)(B) S10=500+450=950S_{10} = 500 + 450 = 950S10​=500+450=950; the 10th day alone: a10=140a_{10} = 140a10​=140.

  6. Check: S25−S24=(3125+1125)−(2880+1080)=4250−3960=290S_{25} - S_{24} = (3125 + 1125) - (2880 + 1080) = 4250 - 3960 = 290S25​−S24​=(3125+1125)−(2880+1080)=4250−3960=290 ✔.

  7. Answer (i) 50 (ii) an=10n+40a_n = 10n + 40an​=10n+40 (iii)(A) the 25th day — OR — (iii)(B) 950 visitors in 10 days; 140 on the 10th day

    Common trap: In (iii)(A), solving 5n2+45n=2905n^2 + 45n = 2905n2+45n=290: that asks when the total reaches 290.

Concept used: Sn=n2(a+l)S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l)Sn​=2n​(a+l), then l=a+(n−1)dl = a + (n - 1)dl=a+(n−1)d (Topic 4). Why it applies: first and last terms are known.

  1. 1

    120=n2(−5+45)=20n120 = \dfrac{n}{2}(-5 + 45) = 20n120=2n​(−5+45)=20n, so n=6n = 6n=6.

  2. 2

    45=−5+5d45 = -5 + 5d45=−5+5d, so 5d=505d = 505d=50 and d=10d = 10d=10.

  3. Check: −5,5,15,25,35,45-5, 5, 15, 25, 35, 45−5,5,15,25,35,45 add up to 120 ✔.

  4. Answer n=6n = 6n=6, d=10d = 10d=10

    Common trap: Using 6d6d6d instead of 5d5d5d in step 2.

In an AP, if Sn=3n2+5nS_n = 3n^2 + 5nSn​=3n2+5n and ak=164a_k = 164ak​=164, find the value of k.

Full solution

Given: Sn=3n2+5nS_n = 3n^2 + 5nSn​=3n2+5n, ak=164a_k = 164ak​=164. Asked: k.

Concept used: an=Sn−Sn−1a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}an​=Sn​−Sn−1​ (Topic 4). Why it applies: the sum formula is given; a term is asked.

  1. 1

    Sn−1=3(n−1)2+5(n−1)=3n2−n−2S_{n-1} = 3(n - 1)^2 + 5(n - 1) = 3n^2 - n - 2Sn−1​=3(n−1)2+5(n−1)=3n2−n−2.

  2. 2

    an=(3n2+5n)−(3n2−n−2)=6n+2a_n = (3n^2 + 5n) - (3n^2 - n - 2) = 6n + 2an​=(3n2+5n)−(3n2−n−2)=6n+2.

  3. 3

    6k+2=1646k + 2 = 1646k+2=164, so 6k=1626k = 1626k=162 and k=27k = 27k=27.

  4. Check: S27−S26=(2187+135)−(2028+130)=2322−2158=164S_{27} - S_{26} = (2187 + 135) - (2028 + 130) = 2322 - 2158 = 164S27​−S26​=(2187+135)−(2028+130)=2322−2158=164 ✔.

  5. Answer k=27k = 27k=27

    Common trap: Solving 3k2+5k=1643k^2 + 5k = 1643k2+5k=164 — that sets the sum equal to 164.

E15●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 5, Ex 5.3 Q32

How many terms of the AP: −15,−13,−11,…-15, -13, -11, \ldots−15,−13,−11,… are needed to make the sum −55-55−55? Explain the reason for double answer.

Full solution

Given: a=−15a = -15a=−15, d=2d = 2d=2, Sn=−55S_n = -55Sn​=−55. Asked: n and the reason for two answers.

Concept used: quadratic in n; both roots can be valid (Topic 4). Why it applies: the terms change sign from negative to positive.

  1. 1

    −55=n2[−30+2(n−1)]=n(n−16)-55 = \dfrac{n}{2}[-30 + 2(n - 1)] = n(n - 16)−55=2n​[−30+2(n−1)]=n(n−16).

  2. 2

    Rearrange: n2−16n+55=0n^2 - 16n + 55 = 0n2−16n+55=0, so (n−5)(n−11)=0(n - 5)(n - 11) = 0(n−5)(n−11)=0.

  3. 3

    n=5n = 5n=5 or n=11n = 11n=11 — both positive whole numbers.

  4. 4

    Reason: the 6th to 11th terms are −5,−3,−1,1,3,5-5, -3, -1, 1, 3, 5−5,−3,−1,1,3,5, which add up to 0, so the sum is −55-55−55 after 5 terms and again after 11 terms.

  5. Check: S5=52(−15−7)=−55S_5 = \dfrac{5}{2}(-15 - 7) = -55S5​=25​(−15−7)=−55 ✔ and S11=112(−15+5)=−55S_{11} = \dfrac{11}{2}(-15 + 5) = -55S11​=211​(−15+5)=−55 ✔.

  6. Answer 5 or 11 terms; terms 6 to 11 cancel out.

    Common trap: Rejecting one root without a reason.

E16●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 5, Ex 5.3 Q35

Yasmeen saves Rs 32 during the first month, Rs 36 in the second month and Rs 40 in the third month. If she continues to save in this manner, in how many months will she save Rs 2000?

Full solution

Given: monthly savings 32,36,40,…32, 36, 40, \ldots32,36,40,…: a=32a = 32a=32, d=4d = 4d=4; total ₹ 2000. Asked: n.

Concept used: "save Rs 2000" in all → a total → SnS_nSn​ (Topic 5). Why it applies: one term = one month's saving.

  1. 1

    2000=n2[64+4(n−1)]=n2(4n+60)=n(2n+30)2000 = \dfrac{n}{2}[64 + 4(n - 1)] = \dfrac{n}{2}(4n + 60) = n(2n + 30)2000=2n​[64+4(n−1)]=2n​(4n+60)=n(2n+30).

  2. 2

    Divide by 2: n2+15n−1000=0n^2 + 15n - 1000 = 0n2+15n−1000=0, so (n+40)(n−25)=0(n + 40)(n - 25) = 0(n+40)(n−25)=0.

  3. 3

    n=−40n = -40n=−40 is impossible, so n=25n = 25n=25.

  4. Check: S25=252[64+96]=25×80=2000S_{25} = \dfrac{25}{2}[64 + 96] = 25 \times 80 = 2000S25​=225​[64+96]=25×80=2000 ✔.

E17●●● AdvancedShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 5, Ex 5.4 Q2

Find the
(i) sum of those integers between 1 and 500 which are multiples of 2 as well as of 5.
(ii) sum of those integers from 1 to 500 which are multiples of 2 as well as of 5.
(iii) sum of those integers from 1 to 500 which are multiples of 2 or 5.
[Hint (iii) : These numbers will be : multiples of 2 + multiples of 5 – multiples of 2 as well as of 5]

Full solution

Given: the integers 1 to 500. Asked: three sums.

Concept used: multiples of both 2 and 5 are multiples of LCM=10\text{LCM} = 10LCM=10; "or" = (multiples of 2) + (multiples of 5) − (multiples of 10) (Topic 4). Why it applies: each set of multiples is an AP.

  1. 1

    (i) "Between 1 and 500" excludes 500: 10,20,…,49010, 20, \ldots, 49010,20,…,490 — 49 terms; sum 492(10+490)=12250\dfrac{49}{2}(10 + 490) = 12250249​(10+490)=12250.

  2. 2

    (ii) "From 1 to 500" includes 500: 10,…,50010, \ldots, 50010,…,500 — 50 terms; sum 25×510=1275025 \times 510 = 1275025×510=12750.

  3. 3

    (iii) Multiples of 2: 2+4+⋯+500=250×251=627502 + 4 + \cdots + 500 = 250 \times 251 = 627502+4+⋯+500=250×251=62750. Multiples of 5: 5+⋯+500=50×505=252505 + \cdots + 500 = 50 \times 505 = 252505+⋯+500=50×505=25250.

  4. 4

    Subtract the multiples of 10 (counted twice): 62750+25250−12750=7525062750 + 25250 - 12750 = 7525062750+25250−12750=75250.

  5. Check: (ii) − (i) =500= 500=500, the one extra number ✔.

  6. Answer (i) 12250 (ii) 12750 (iii) 75250

    Common trap: In (iii), adding the two sums without subtracting the multiples of 10, which counts 10, 20, … twice.

E18●●● AdvancedShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 5, Ex 5.4 Q4

An AP consists of 37 terms. The sum of the three middle most terms is 225 and the sum of the last three is 429. Find the AP.

Full solution

Given: n=37n = 37n=37; the three middle terms add to 225; the last three add to 429. Asked: the AP.

Concept used: with 37 terms the middle term is the 19th; three consecutive terms add to 3 times the middle one (Topic 3). Why it applies: (b−d)+b+(b+d)=3b(b - d) + b + (b + d) = 3b(b−d)+b+(b+d)=3b.

  1. 1

    Middle three: a18+a19+a20=3a19=225a_{18} + a_{19} + a_{20} = 3a_{19} = 225a18​+a19​+a20​=3a19​=225, so a19=75a_{19} = 75a19​=75.

  2. 2

    Last three: a35+a36+a37=3a36=429a_{35} + a_{36} + a_{37} = 3a_{36} = 429a35​+a36​+a37​=3a36​=429, so a36=143a_{36} = 143a36​=143.

  3. 3

    From the 19th to the 36th term: 17d=143−75=6817d = 143 - 75 = 6817d=143−75=68, so d=4d = 4d=4.

  4. 4

    a=a19−18d=75−72=3a = a_{19} - 18d = 75 - 72 = 3a=a19​−18d=75−72=3.

  5. Check: a18+a19+a20=71+75+79=225a_{18} + a_{19} + a_{20} = 71 + 75 + 79 = 225a18​+a19​+a20​=71+75+79=225 ✔; a35+a36+a37=139+143+147=429a_{35} + a_{36} + a_{37} = 139 + 143 + 147 = 429a35​+a36​+a37​=139+143+147=429 ✔.

  6. Answer 3,7,11,15,…3, 7, 11, 15, \ldots3,7,11,15,…

    Common trap: Taking the 18th term as the middle of 37 terms. The middle is the 37+12=19\dfrac{37 + 1}{2} = 19237+1​=19th.

C1 — Case: TV sets from a factory●● StandardCase/source-based · 5 marksCBSE Mathematics Class X Case Study Question Bank, Arithmetic Progression, Case Study 1

India is competitive manufacturing location due to the low cost of manpower and strong technical and engineering capabilities contributing to higher quality production runs. The production of TV sets in a factory increases uniformly by a fixed number every year. It produced 16000 sets in 6 th year and 22600 in 9th year.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

  1. Find the production during first year.
  2. Find the production during 8th year.
  3. Find the production during first 3 years.
  4. In which year, the production is Rs 29,200.
  5. Find the difference of the production during 7th year and 4th year.

(The bank's question 4 and its answer 1 say "Rs", but the quantities are numbers of TV sets.)

Full solution

Given: a6=16000a_6 = 16000a6​=16000, a9=22600a_9 = 22600a9​=22600 (sets). Asked: five answers.

Concept used: two terms give a and d; then terms and a short sum (Topics 3–5). Why it applies: "increases uniformly by a fixed number" makes the yearly production an AP.

  1. 1

    3d=22600−16000=66003d = 22600 - 16000 = 66003d=22600−16000=6600, so d=2200d = 2200d=2200.

  2. 2

    a=a6−5d=16000−11000=5000a = a_6 - 5d = 16000 - 11000 = 5000a=a6​−5d=16000−11000=5000.

  3. 3

    Part 1: 5000 sets.

  4. 4

    Part 2: a8=5000+7×2200=20400a_8 = 5000 + 7 \times 2200 = 20400a8​=5000+7×2200=20400.

  5. 5

    Part 3: 5000+7200+9400=216005000 + 7200 + 9400 = 216005000+7200+9400=21600 (or S3=32(5000+9400)S_3 = \dfrac{3}{2}(5000 + 9400)S3​=23​(5000+9400)).

  6. 6

    Part 4: 29200=5000+2200(n−1)29200 = 5000 + 2200(n - 1)29200=5000+2200(n−1), so 24200=2200(n−1)24200 = 2200(n - 1)24200=2200(n−1), n−1=11n - 1 = 11n−1=11, n=12n = 12n=12.

  7. 7

    Part 5: a7−a4=3d=6600a_7 - a_4 = 3d = 6600a7​−a4​=3d=6600 (that is, 18200−1160018200 - 1160018200−11600).

  8. Check: a9=5000+8×2200=22600a_9 = 5000 + 8 \times 2200 = 22600a9​=5000+8×2200=22600 ✔.

  9. Answer

    1. 5000 sets 2. 20400 3. 21600 4. the 12th year 5. 6600

    Common trap: Part 3 asks for the total of three years, not the 3rd year's production (9400). (The bank's worked answer to part 2 prints "5000 + 2(2200)"; the correct working is 5000+7×22005000 + 7 \times 22005000+7×2200, which gives its stated 20400.)

Your friend Veer wants to participate in a 200m race. He can currently run that distance in 51 seconds and with each day of practice it takes him 2 seconds less.He wants to do in 31 seconds .

  1. Which of the following terms are in AP for the given situation

a) 51,53,55…. b) 51, 49, 47…. c) -51, -53, -55…. d) 51, 55, 59…

  1. Which of the following term is not in the AP of the above given situation

a) 41 b) 30 c) 37 d) 39

  1. If nth term of an AP is given by an=2n+3a_n = 2n + 3an​=2n+3 then common difference of an AP is

a) 2 b) 3 c) 5 d) 1

  1. The value of x, for which 2x, x+ 10, 3x + 2 are three consecutive terms of an AP

a) 6 b) -6 c) 18 d) -18

(The bank's picture shows a runner on a track. The bank's question 2, "the minimum number of days he needs to practice", is left out: it can be read as 10 days of practice — from 51 s to 31 s is 10 steps of 2 s — or, as the bank's key does, 11 days counting the first day's 51-second run; both are printed as options.)

Full solution

Given: times 51,49,47,…51, 49, 47, \ldots51,49,47,… seconds: a=51a = 51a=51, d=−2d = -2d=−2. Asked: four answers.

Concept used: AP terms, which term, AP test, d from ana_nan​, 2b=a+c2b = a + c2b=a+c (Topics 2–3). Why it applies: the time falls by the same 2 s each day.

  1. 1

    Part 1: the times go down by 2 → (b) 51,49,47,…51, 49, 47, \ldots51,49,47,…

  2. 2

    Part 2: every term 51−2(n−1)51 - 2(n - 1)51−2(n−1) is odd; 30 is even → (b).

  3. 3

    Part 3: an+1−an=2a_{n+1} - a_n = 2an+1​−an​=2 → (a).

  4. 4

    Part 4: 2(x+10)=2x+(3x+2)2(x + 10) = 2x + (3x + 2)2(x+10)=2x+(3x+2), so 2x+20=5x+22x + 20 = 5x + 22x+20=5x+2, 3x=183x = 183x=18, x=6x = 6x=6 → (a).

  5. Check: part 4: 12,16,2012, 16, 2012,16,20 — differences 4, 4 ✔.

  6. Answer

    1. (b) 2. (b) 30 3. (a) 2 4. (a) 6

    Common trap: In part 1, choosing (a) 51,53,55,…51, 53, 55, \ldots51,53,55,… — practice makes the time go down, so d=−2d = -2d=−2.

Your elder brother wants to buy a car and plans to take loan from a bank for his car. He repays his total loan of Rs 1,18,000 by paying every month starting with the first instalment of Rs 1000. If he increases the instalment by Rs 100 every month , answer the following:

    Part 3: 118000−73500=44500118000 - 73500 = 44500118000−73500=44500 → (c).

    Part 4: a40=1000+39×100=4900a_{40} = 1000 + 39 \times 100 = 4900a40​=1000+39×100=4900 → (a).

    Part 5: 1000:4900=10:491000 : 4900 = 10 : 491000:4900=10:49 → (b).

    1. (a) 2. (b) 3. (c) 4. (a) 5. (b)
